posts.cooked: I feel SSH and Networking commands are not covered in detail in professor’s lecture and the live session. posts.name: Swati Jain
posts.cooked: You can join tomorrow’s TA session I’ll go through the SSH. Meanwhile, you can refer to this SSH command usage, options, and configuration in Linux/Unix (non-course resource).

posts.name: Pratosh Lathia
posts.cooked:
I watched week 2 lectures but the content isn’t sufficient to answer the Graded Assignment questions

10001066301440×3007 302 KB

There is nothing related to these questions as discussed in professor’s lecture

Any help on how to solve?

@sayan @hemalatha

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked: Questions wont always come directly from the lectures in diploma/degree level. Students are expected to watch the lecture as the introduction/motivation to the topic and then learn a bit more about it themselves online. These graded questions are aimed to make you explore the topic yourself with the help of the questions. Try to find out the answers using online resources.

posts.name: Pratosh Lathia
posts.cooked:
We still haven’t learned how to setup a ssh server

How can I learn which error I’ll get if I can’t practice it anywhere

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
You already have got access to a ssh server from the start of the course, please refer to Course VM Login Process > VM Login Instructions.

Once you have gained the normal access, feel free to play around with the different scenarios mentioned in the graded assignment by manipulating the key / known_hosts file.
